snapshot_markdown:
**Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC)** — Precious Metals and Minerals Mining, Perth, AU. 1,127 employees. The largest rare-earth producer outside China. Owns the Mount Weld deposit (WA) and processing facilities in Kalgoorlie + Malaysia. Only producer of separated heavy rare-earth dysprosium and terbium outside China.

### Situational read
Profitable and scaling hard. Geopolitical tailwinds are absurd: 10-year Malaysian license renewal, revamped Japan supply deal, US$96M DoW offtake with price floor, Vietnam partnership, samarium production milestone. Just raised AU$750M (Aug 2025) plus another AU$75M SPP in progress to fund the Towards 2030 strategy: downstream metal and magnet supply chain expansion. Capex heavy at -$342M TTM. Stock up 197% YoY. **Two operational pressure flags worth pitching against:** (1) CEO Amanda Lacaze retiring June 2026 after 12 years — leadership inflection point. (2) Late-2025 Kalgoorlie power outage caused significant production loss, surfaced infrastructure vulnerability.

### Financials (USD, TTM ending Dec 31, 2025)
- Market Cap **$14.45B** (+197% YoY), Enterprise Value **$13.90B** (+190% YoY)
- Total Revenue **$452.4M** (+42% YoY), Gross Margin **38.8%**, EBITDA **$122.2M** (+76% YoY)
- EV/Revenue 30.7x, EV/EBITDA 113.8x — priced for execution
- Total Assets **$2.67B**, Total Debt **$142.4M**, Total Equity **$2.25B**, D/E 0.06 — equity-funded growth, very low leverage

### Capital structure
$784M raised to date. Mostly equity-financed. Anchor recent deals: **$486.7M PIPE Aug 2025** (AU$750M) + $48.7M SPP in progress. March 2023 Japan Australia Rare Earths PIPE $146.3M, Aug 2020 Kalgoorlie expansion PIPE $151.2M. Hancock Prospecting holds 5.82% (since Apr 2024). No bank debt syndicate — projects funded through equity + government partnerships.

### Recent activity (last 6 months)
Avalanche of expansion news: US DoW supply deal (Mar), Japan deal extension (Mar), Vietnam metal-making JV with LS Eco (Mar), Malaysian samarium production milestone (Mar), 10-year Malaysian license renewal. April: higher Q3 sales reported, JPMorgan exited substantial position. **CEO retirement announced** for June 2026. Western Australia power outage (Nov 2025) flagged as operational risk.

### Top contacts for outreach
1. **Gaudenz Sturzenegger** — CFO — gsturzenegger@lynascorp.com
2. **Pol Roux** — COO — pr@lynascorp.com (operational pain owner)
3. **Daniel Havas** — VP Strategy & IR — daniel.havas@lynascorp.com

Main line: +61 (0)8 6241 3800. Note: Amanda Lacaze is the listed primary contact in PitchBook but is **retiring June 2026** — deprioritize.

### Why they'd buy
Massive simultaneous build-out across three continents (Malaysia, Vietnam, US, WA Kalgoorlie ramp). CEO transition window = appetite for outside operational frameworks. Recent power outage exposed infrastructure resilience gaps in core production site. Growing 1,127-person org from a 998-person base with downstream complexity (metal + magnet) they've never operated before. Heavy capex + government counterparty oversight (US DoW, Japanese government deals) = operational maturity demands rising fast. Pitch the COO.
